description: RenderJob retry semantics diverge: ADR-026 and target/closeout doc state 'retry creates a new RenderJob'. Platform coordination blueprint states 'POST retry → reset status to PENDING, reset attempt_count' (row reset). Backend integrity audit confirms the actual RenderJobService.retry() resets the same row to QUEUED, violating the one-attempt rule. The retry route was removed as LIFECYCLE_SEMANTICS_INVALID but the blueprint still documents the reset-row behavior as the recovery API.
accepted_rule: RenderJob = one execution attempt. Retry = new RenderJob with provenance link. FALLBACKING/RETRYING states excluded.
current_effect: Blueprint documents a retry API that resets rows. Implementation had this behavior. ADR-026 says new RenderJob. Agent developers reading the blueprint will implement row-reset retry, violating the architecture rule.

description: ADR-026 proposes adding render_job.updated_at and render_job.idempotency_key as V5 schema changes. The actual V1__init_full_schema.sql render_job table has NO updated_at column — only created_at. Other tables (platform_job, platform_task) do have updated_at. The render_job table is missing this column in the running schema. ADR-026 calls this 'MINIMUM_V5_REQUIRED' but V5 is quarantined per frozen rules.
accepted_rule: V1-V4 frozen. V5 quarinated. RenderJob schema changes deferred to V5 implementation.
current_effect: render_job table has no updated_at column. Any code that reads/writes render_job.updated_at will fail against the current schema. The column only exists in ADR-026 target-state, not in any applied migration.

description: ADR-025 explicitly defers Artifact DAG indefinitely. However, execution-planner.md still lists 'Artifact DAG (what needs to be produced)' as a pipeline input (line 30), shows 'Phase 1: Artifact DAG model (Sprint 047)' in roadmap (line 149), and has 'Load Artifact DAG' as step 1 of the execution flow (line 97). While disclaimers exist, the diagrams and flow steps present Artifact DAG as a current or near-term pipeline component.
accepted_rule: Artifact DAG is indefinitely deferred (ADR-025). Not a dependency for any current work item. Retained only as extension layer vocabulary.
current_effect: Developers and agents reading execution-planner.md see Artifact DAG as a pipeline step, potentially scheduling implementation work against it despite the deferral.

description: Creative-planner.md shows the full pipeline flow as 'TimelineEditPlan → TimelineMutationService → TimelineRevision → Review/Merge → Execution Planner → Artifact DAG → Render/Export' (line 18). Artifact DAG appears as a required step in the render pipeline. A disclaimer exists but the diagram is misleading as a pipeline dependency.
accepted_rule: Artifact DAG is indefinitely deferred. Current render pipeline does not include Artifact DAG.
current_effect: Pipeline diagram implies Artifact DAG is between Execution Planner and Render, which is factually wrong for current production.

description: System architecture overview (01-system-architecture.md) references 'Frontend (Vue 3)' in the architecture diagram (line 13). Frontend architecture document (04-frontend-architecture.md) explicitly states 'React-first migration' with React 19, and says 'The previous Vue 3 frontend was a separate application. This is a new project. There is no existing Vue code to maintain compatibility with.' The system architecture diagram is stale.
accepted_rule: Frontend is React-first (React 19 + Remotion). Vue 3 is not carried forward.
current_effect: New developers or agents reading the system architecture overview will believe the frontend uses Vue 3, causing confusion when they encounter React code.

description: Two completely different ADRs share the identifier ADR-026. The architecture/adr version is 'Render Output Commit Protocol' (PROPOSED status). The render/adr version is 'Phase 2b High-Autonomy Feature Completion Mode' (ACCEPTED status, 2026-07-01). Same ADR number, different domains, different content, different statuses.
accepted_rule: ADR numbers must be unique across the entire project. No two ADRs may share the same identifier.
current_effect: Any reference to 'ADR-026' is ambiguous. Agents and developers cannot determine which document is intended. The render/adr ADR-026 is accepted while the architecture/adr ADR-026 is proposed — they have contradictory authority claims.

description: ADR-016b has title '# ADR-016: Execution Lifecycle' (line 8) — it uses the same ADR-016 identifier as ADR-016-execution-job-model.md. The file is named ADR-016b but the document title says ADR-016. Both are status: accepted. They cover different topics (Job Model vs Lifecycle) but share the ADR-016 identifier.
accepted_rule: ADR numbers must be unique. ADR-016b should have its own distinct identifier.
current_effect: References to 'ADR-016' are ambiguous — could mean Execution Job Model or Execution Lifecycle.

description: ADR-001 through ADR-007 exist in BOTH docs/architecture/adr/ and docs/render/adr/ directories with different content. Architecture/adr ADR-005 is 'Extension Decision Guide' while render/adr ADR-001 is 'Render Provider Classification'. The numbering namespaces overlap: render/adr/ADR-005 is 'LiteFlow Workflow Orchestration' while architecture/adr/ADR-005 is 'Extension Decision Guide'.
accepted_rule: ADR numbers must be globally unique or use explicit namespace prefixes.
current_effect: ADR-005 in architecture/adr means Extension Decision Guide. ADR-005 in render/adr means LiteFlow Workflow Orchestration. Same number, completely different decisions.

description: ADR-026 proposes V5 adds render_output_commit and render_output_item tables. The data architecture document (06-data-architecture.md) shows a completely different V5: 'V5__outbox_audit_enhancements.sql — (alters) outbox_events, audit_records'. The archive has yet another V5: 'V5__add_artifact_size_bytes_and_checksum.sql'. Three different V5 definitions exist across documents.
accepted_rule: V1-V4 frozen. V5 is quarantined. Flyway migration history is the source of truth for applied schemas.
current_effect: Three conflicting definitions of what V5 contains. No V5 migration is applied. Agents cannot determine which V5 definition is authoritative.

description: ADR-026 header says status: PROPOSED. The target closeout document says 'Status: ACCEPTED'. The Agent A inventory notes say 'Status: accepted'. ADR-026 is the canonical architecture decision record but its own status field says PROPOSED while downstream documents treat it as accepted.
accepted_rule: ADR status must be consistent. If accepted, the ADR itself must say accepted.
current_effect: Agents cannot determine if ADR-026 is binding (accepted) or still under review (proposed). Downstream documents assume accepted but the source says proposed.

description: The OpenAPI spec (openapi-preview-current.json) likely contains retry endpoint definitions (the spec is large and covers render jobs). The backend integrity audit document states the retry route was REMOVED as LIFECYCLE_SEMANTICS_INVALID. If the OpenAPI spec still includes POST /render/jobs/{jobId}/retry, it conflicts with the removal decision.
accepted_rule: Retry route removed. RenderJob one-attempt rule. No retry endpoint in canonical API.
current_effect: API consumers may attempt to call a retry endpoint that no longer exists or was never properly implemented.

description: Multiple target-state documents under docs/architecture/target/ describe render_output_commit protocol implementation details (verification contract, implementation roadmap, closeout). These reference V5 schema changes that are quarantined and unimplemented. The target-state documents describe a system that does not exist yet, creating confusion about current capabilities.
accepted_rule: Target-state documents must be clearly labeled and not confused with current-state documentation.
current_effect: Agents reading target-state docs may believe render_output_commit protocol is implemented.

description: Multiple ADRs lack owner metadata. ADR-022, ADR-023, ADR-024, ADR-025, ADR-026 have no 'created' date and no 'owner' field in their YAML frontmatter (some lack frontmatter entirely). ADR-025 and ADR-026 have no YAML frontmatter at all. The data architecture doc (06-data-architecture.md) has 'Last Updated: 2026-05-18' but no owner or status.
accepted_rule: All authoritative documents should have owner, status, and version/date metadata.
current_effect: Cannot determine who owns or maintains these documents. Cannot determine if they are current.

description: Backend integrity audit removed the retry route and documented that RenderJob retry is LIFECYCLE_SEMANTICS_INVALID. However, task-dispatcher-runtime.md still shows 'check canRetry → retry or FAILED' in its flow diagram (line 52). PlatformTask.canRetry() is a different entity from RenderJob retry, but the canRetry concept creates ambiguity about which retry semantics apply.
accepted_rule: RenderJob: no retry (one attempt, new job). PlatformTask: canRetry() is valid (attempt_count < max_attempts). These are different entities with different rules.
current_effect: Developers may confuse PlatformTask retry semantics with RenderJob retry semantics.

description: The data architecture ER diagram shows 'render_job ||--o| artifact : produces' — implying one-to-one RenderJob-to-Artifact. ADR-026 introduces RenderOutputCommit as intermediary with RenderOutputItem children. The current schema has artifact_uri directly on render_job. The ER diagram and ADR-026 describe different data models for the render output relationship.
accepted_rule: Current production: render_job.artifact_uri direct reference. Target (V5): render_output_commit as intermediary.
current_effect: ER diagram shows current model. ADR-026 shows target model. Neither explicitly states which is current vs target.

description: current-phase.md lists completed items and current priorities for 'Capability Production Era'. Backend integrity documents say 'Backend capability expansion remains PAUSED' and 'Frontend feature development remains frozen'. The handoff doc implies forward momentum while integrity docs describe a frozen state. The kanban task for this inventory (t_82581ccd) has lifecycle_state 'done' — but the task is still executing (Agent C is running now).
accepted_rule: Kanban 'done' state should mean task completed. Current-phase doc should reflect actual system state.
current_effect: Confusion about whether the platform is actively developing or frozen.

description: ADR-005 appears twice with different content: architecture/adr/ADR-005 is 'Extension Decision Guide' (status: accepted) and render/adr/ADR-005 is 'LiteFlow Workflow Orchestration'. Both claim the ADR-005 identifier. Additionally, architecture/adr/ADR-009 is 'Artifact Runtime (status: superseded by ADR-010)' — the only ADR with explicit supersession, creating a lifecycle pattern not applied to other conflicts.
accepted_rule: ADR numbering must be globally unique. Supersession must be explicit and consistent.
current_effect: ADR-005 reference is ambiguous across the entire project.

description: Two schema definitions exist: docs/ddl-postgresql.sql (which self-identifies as '非权威参考草案（NOT SOURCE OF TRUTH）') uses named schemas (core.*, render.*, ai.*) with UUID primary keys. V1__init_full_schema.sql uses public schema with varchar(64) primary keys. They define completely different table structures for the same entities. The DDL doc is explicitly not authoritative but exists as a reference that can mislead.
accepted_rule: Flyway migrations are source of truth. DDL file is explicitly not authoritative.
current_effect: Agents or developers referencing docs/ddl-postgresql.sql will see a schema that doesn't match the actual database.

description: Execution-planner.md lists 'Phase 1: Artifact DAG model (Sprint 047)' as future work (line 149). ADR-025 says 'All P3A.x items are conditional, not committed roadmap' and 'Artifact DAG is removed from near-term roadmap'. The Sprint 047 reference in execution-planner implies a scheduled delivery, contradicting ADR-025's explicit deferral.
accepted_rule: Artifact DAG has no scheduled sprint. All future work is conditional on measured production need.
current_effect: Sprint reference creates false impression of scheduled implementation.

description: ADR-026 status is PROPOSED but downstream documents treat it as ACCEPTED. No governance process or document lifecycle policy enforcement caught this status discrepancy. The document lifecycle policy exists but did not prevent the ADR from being referenced as accepted while its own header says proposed.
accepted_rule: Document lifecycle policy should enforce status consistency across references.
current_effect: Governance gap: status discrepancies propagate unchecked.

description: ADR-026 specifies render_output_commit and render_output_item as new tables. V1__init_full_schema.sql has no such tables. The current schema has render_job.artifact_uri as a direct text field. The ADR-026 completion invariant requires 7 conditions (render_output COMMITTED, StorageReference exists, Artifact READY, Product READY, RenderBillingRecord exists, lifecycle event) — none of these tables/conditions exist in V1-V4.
accepted_rule: Current schema: render_job.artifact_uri. Target schema: render_output_commit protocol. V5 required but quarantined.
current_effect: ADR-026 describes a system that cannot exist without V5. V5 is quarantined. The protocol is unimplementable in current schema.
